paragraphs: He is mentioned in Tanchuma, Shelach 3, and in Bemidbar Rabbah, chapter 16, section 3, and in the Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot chapter 2, end of halakhah 4: R' Lia, R' Yasa, in the name of R' Acha Rubah.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Rubah is Aramaic great/elder; its relation to the headed the Great is Hyman’s grouping, not independently established identity. Lia/Yasa follow supplied forms, with all four personal-title occurrences R'. The separately read Wikisource witness lacks the heading and reads דובה where the frozen full scan-text witness has רובה; neither is silently harmonized.

ובמ״ר is contextually Bemidbar Rabbah from the Shelach parallel; alternative division and-in-Midrash-Rabbah leaves the book unnamed. פט״ז-ג gives 16:3, סה״ד end of halakhah 4 in Berakhot chapter 2, not final halakhah. No new named-edition check is claimed.
